3.2.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "how do you template a total hip?"
- "Calibrate → films magnified ≈20% → **marker** of known size at hip level."
- "Cup → native **hip centre**, lower edge at teardrop, medial edge on ilio-ischial line, **45°**."
- "Stem → shaft axis, canal fill, **neck cut** from lesser trochanter → **leg length** and **offset**."

### Spotorno index — stem fixation score
| Item (Handbook) | Finding → points |
|---|---|
| **MCI** (morphological cortical index) = outer diameter at lesser trochanter ÷ canal 7 cm below | >3 → 0 · 2.7–3.0 → 1 · 2.3–2.6 → 2 · <2.3 → 4 |
| **Sex** | male 0 · female 1 |
| **Age** | <50 → 0 · 50–60 → 1 · 60–70 → 2 · >70 → 3 |
| **Singh index** | grade 6 → 0 · 5 → 1 · 3–4 → 2 · 1–2 → 4 |

- Total → **≤4 cementless · 5 discuss · ≥6 cemented** (Handbook)
- Bone items score up to 4 each → can outweigh age and sex
- **Singh index** → trabecular groups vanish: secondary first, principal compressive last
[[FIG: Fig 3.13 · 3.2
- Guides the **stem** only → cup fixation decided separately

### Limb-length discrepancy
#### Reading the film
- Horizontal line, square to the body axis → to the top of each **lesser trochanter** → difference = LLD
[[FIG: Fig 3.14 · 3.2

| Line | Landmark | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| **Interischial** | ischial tuberosities → easier | harder → miscalculation risk |
| **Inter-teardrop** | teardrops → harder | easier → direct subtraction |

#### Film vs clinical
- **Apparent** shortening → pelvic obliquity, scoliosis → the spine may be the cause
[[FIG: Fig 3.15 · 3.2
- True = **ASIS** (anterior superior iliac spine) → medial malleolus · apparent = umbilicus → medial malleolus
- **Fixed flexion** → sound limb in the same flexion · **block test** → pelvis levelled on blocks
[[FIG: Fig 3.16 · 3.2
- Fixed **adduction** looks short → correcting to the film alone **overlengthens** → always pair film and clinic

#### Why a few millimetres matter
- Normal people → **5–15 mm**, unaware if <1 cm (Prof Fawzy)
- After THA → within 1 cm 72% · >1 cm long **22%** · >1 cm short ≈8% (Prof Fawzy)
- Results → revision, litigation · USA → compensation + **punitive damages**
- Acceptable → within **1 cm** (Charnley) → examine, plan, measure and adjust in theatre

#### Causes, effects & types
- Pre-op causes → **acetabular erosion**, head collapse, subluxation, fixed deformity
[[FIG: Fig 3.17 · 3.2
- Effects → **limp**, shoe raise, pelvic obliquity, compensatory scoliosis, tiptoeing
[[FIG: Fig 3.18 · 3.2
- Longer side → knee flexion, **abductor strain**
[[FIG: Fig 3.19 · 3.2
- **Shortening** → **dislocation** · short head, high cup, deep stem, mainly offset not restored
[[FIG: Fig 3.20 · 3.2

CLINICAL PEARL — two types of LLD after THA (Prof Fawzy)
- **Type 1** → component-related: stem proud, cup high or low, neck cut
- **Type 2** → malposition → long neck chosen for stability

[[FIG: Fig 3.21 · 3.2

### Acetabular templating
#### Preparing the film
- **Software** or transparent sheet · every film is magnified ≈**20%** (Campbell)
- Digital → **calibration marker** of known size at hip level → magnified like the hip
[[FIG: Fig 3.22 · 3.2
- Plan → standard vs **high-offset** stem, stem depth, cup size, coverage, insertion level
[[FIG: Fig 3.23 · 3.2

#### Seating the cup
- **Hip centre** = where ilio-ischial line, ilio-pubic line and teardrop meet · distances copied from the other side
[[FIG: Fig 3.24 · 3.2
- Native centre restored → offset and leg length derive from it · cup centre = hip centre
- Template centre on X-ray centre · **lower edge at teardrop** · **medial edge** on the ilio-ischial line
- Too medial → breaches the floor · too lateral → uncovered

#### Angle & mantle
- **Inclination 45°** to the horizontal · bone missing over the template = deficient bone (Prof Hazem)
- Cemented → **≈3 mm** mantle allowance, PMMA (polymethyl methacrylate) spacers 3 mm high (Campbell) · cementless → none
[[FIG: Fig 3.25 · 3.2
- **Dysplasia** → superolateral rim uncovered → medialise, augment or smaller cup, not a high centre

- Femoral cement mantle → 2 Fixation

### Femoral templating
#### Aligning the stem
- Template axis = **femoral shaft axis** · tip centred in the medulla: equal gaps to both cortices
- **Neck–stem junction** at the osteotomy → greater trochanter tip to 1 fingerbreadth above lesser trochanter
- Theatre → measure **lesser trochanter → neck saddle** → reproduces the planned cut (Campbell)

#### Neck cut & leg length
- Head centre **1 cm above** hip centre → leg **+1 cm** · stem 9 mm higher → +9 mm (Prof Gobba)
[[FIG: Fig 3.26 · 3.2
- Size, cut and head centre interlinked → lower cut drops the head centre → shorter leg

#### Choosing the design
- Template the **design**, not only size → real offset may exceed the template → change stem
[[FIG: Fig 3.27 · 3.2
- **Coxa valga** → match neck–shaft angle · Egypt stems mostly 135° or 137.5° (Prof Sherif Khaled)
[[FIG: Fig 3.28 · 3.2
- Wrong angle → wrong offset → limp · needed stem unavailable → **wait**
- Each company → standard + **offset** versions, varised or lateralised → under-offset limps despite equal lengths

HIGH YIELD — Memory line
- **Spotorno ≤4 / ≥6 · LLD ≤1 cm · 20% magnified · teardrop, 45° · head +1 cm = leg +1 cm**

3.3.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "how do you read a post-op THA film?"
- "Six fixed steps → cup **inclination**, cup **offset**, **stem position**, **leg length**, femoral **offset**, **zones**."
- "Targets → inclination 30–50°, **Lewinnek 40 ± 10°** with anteversion **15 ± 10°**, stem central."
- "Compare with the **immediate post-op film** → change over time beats any single number."

### The six steps
| Step | Parameter | Reference |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Cup **inclination** | **theta angle** 30–50° |
| 2 | Cup **offset** | hip centre → teardrop plane |
| 3 | **Stem position** | tip-to-cortex distance |
| 4 | **LLD** | inter-teardrop line → lesser trochanter |
| 5 | Femoral **offset** | hip centre → medullary axis |
| 6 | **Zones** | Gruen (femur) · DeLee–Charnley (cup) |

- Fixed order → no stopping at the first finding · mirrors planning: cup → stem → result
- Cup **anteversion** unreliable on AP → **cross-table lateral** or **CT** (Campbell)
[[FIG: Fig 3.29 · 3.3

### Acetabular inclination — theta angle
- **Theta** = cup face vs horizontal, interischial or inter-teardrop → **30–50°** · template **45°** (Handbook)
- Too steep → edge loading, wear, **metal ions** in metal-on-metal · too flat → neck hits rim in abduction
[[FIG: Fig 3.30 · 3.3
- **DAA** (direct anterior approach) → anteversion 15° from the floor, inclination 40° (Prof Sherif Khaled)
[[FIG: Fig 3.31 · 3.3
- Lewinnek safe zone and which inclination to aim at → 4 Biomechanics

### Acetabular offset
- Hip centre → **teardrop plane**, both sides · longer = **lateralised** · shorter = **medialised**
- Medialising → shorter body-weight lever, lower joint load, slack **abductors** · lateralising → reverse
- Goal → neither → restore the **centre of rotation** (Prof Fawzy)
- Dysplasia → centre restored first → cup stable now and long term

#### Two limits
- Over-reaming medially breaches the **medial wall** → teardrop = the limit
- Lost cup offset → add **femoral offset** → abductors stay tensioned

### Femoral stem position
| Tip | Means | Verdict (Handbook) |
|---|---|---|
| **Central** | equal gaps both sides | normal |
| **Lateral tip** (less lateral gap) | **varus** → lateral bending, instability, loosening, fracture | **not accepted** |
| **Medial tip** (less medial gap) | **valgus** | accepted |

- Varus → longer lever → cemented stems crack and loosen, cementless undersized, subside early · valgus → costs offset
- **Varus** → more offset, shorter leg · **valgus** → less offset, longer leg
[[FIG: Fig 3.32 · 3.3
- Varus usually = **entry too medial** → start toward the greater trochanter before broaching
- Compare **medial (femoral) offset** and **vertical offset** with the other side

### Post-operative leg length
- Same line → top of each lesser trochanter → pre-op LLD corrected?
- Clear difference → neck cut, stem seating or cup height differed → tell the patient early

#### Controlling length in theatre (Prof Fawzy)
- Supine → **square pelvis**, medial malleoli level
[[FIG: Fig 3.33 · 3.3
- Lateral → **traction**, soft-tissue tension, **knee-flexion test**: leg kicks back = too long
- **Steinmann pin** in ilium → greater trochanter tip · navigation · X-ray on trial reduction
[[FIG: Fig 3.34 · 3.3
- **Schanz pin** + sterile ruler → lengthen 2 cm: 9 → 11 cm · DAA → direct view + **Galeazzi** test

#### Already post-op
- Too late → only a **shoe raise** · revision for length alone rarely indicated (Prof Fawzy)
- Early perceived lengthening often settles → pelvic obliquity and abductor spasm resolve

### Femoral offset
- **Femoral (medial) offset** = hip centre → femoral shaft axis
[[FIG: Fig 3.35 · 3.3
- Offset as abductor lever · too little or too much → 4 Biomechanics

#### Restoring it
- Always **imitate** the patient · length need not match if the other hip is diseased (Prof Sherif Khaled)
- **High-offset** (lateralised) stem → offset back without lengthening: head moves medially, not up

### Zones — Gruen & DeLee–Charnley
| Zone | Gruen (femur) | DeLee–Charnley (cup) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | upper ⅓ lateral | superolateral |
| 2 | middle ⅓ lateral | central |
| 3 | lower ⅓ lateral | inferomedial |
| 4 | below the stem tip | — |
| 5 · 6 · 7 | lower · middle · upper ⅓ medial | — |

- Gruen 7 zones · DeLee–Charnley 3 zones (Campbell)
[[FIG: Fig 3.36 · 3.3
- Lateral film → Gruen **14 zones**: 8–14 for anterior and posterior
- Lucency spreading zone to zone on **serial films** = loosening, not one image

HIGH YIELD — Memory line
- **Theta → cup offset → stem tip → LLD → femoral offset → zones · lateral tip = varus = no**
